title: The Bitcoin Age with Nik Bhatia
text: Intro and upcoming events. Alex welcomes attendees to Presidio Bitcoin, introduces Nik Bhatia, and highlights upcoming programming: a bitcoin programming class, a builder event focused on product, UI, and UX, and Presidio Bitcoin Design Week in September. Bitcoin spaces and culture. Nik says Presidio Bitcoin is a special space and compares it with other bitcoin community hubs such as The Commons in Austin and PubKey in New York. He describes bitcoin as uniquely capable of creating coworking spaces where entrepreneurs naturally gather around shared monetary and technical interests.

title: The Bitcoin Age with Nik Bhatia

title: The Bitcoin Age with Nik Bhatia
text: Book tour. Nik discusses publishing The Bitcoin Age after Layered Money and explains that this is his first real book tour. He prefers Q&A over a prepared talk and invites questions on the Fed, power laws, markets, and money. The current Fed's role in markets. Nik says the Fed is mostly irrelevant to his day-to-day market analysis because the interest-rate market continually prices the time value of money across the curve. He watches the 2-year yield closely as a forward indicator of where overnight rates are likely headed over the next one to two years. Market drivers and TBL liquidity index. Nik explains that The Bitcoin Layer built a framework around TBL liquidity. He distinguishes liquidity as market depth from liquidity as money around, then focuses on liquidity as "sheet": the asset side of bank balance sheets. His index combines banking-system assets, interest rates, Treasury volatility, and later the dollar, because more sheet, lower rates, lower volatility, and a weaker dollar all tend to mean stronger market liquidity.

text: Bitcoin's power-law growth. Nik defines a power law as a nonlinear relationship between variables and an exponent, observable in nature and city growth. Nik says the power-law insight that broke his brain was that the exponent of six may be a product of two separate power laws: bitcoin address growth as roughly the square of time, and bitcoin price appreciation as roughly the cube of address growth. He says this framework resonates deeply and will likely guide his research for months or years.

title: 21 in 21: Bradley Axen on Buzz, goose, and AI at Block
text: Haley Berkoe sits down with Bradley Axen, who is leading many of Block's AI initiatives, including Buzz, a new open-source collaboration platform designed for humans and AI agents to work together. He also helped create goose, the open-source AI agent that was later donated to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. Brad also shares his thoughts on where open-source AI is headed, why model flexibility matters, and how new open source AI contributors can get involved. title: 21 in 21: Mic Neale on goose, Mesh LLM, and Open Source AI
text: Mic Neale, a member of the Spiral team at Block and a core developer of goose, an open source AI agent, joins Haley Berkoe on 21 in 21 to discuss goose, Mesh LLM, and open source AI. Mic shares how goose has evolved from a desktop app and CLI into the goose Development Kit (GDK), making it easier for developers to build AI applications. He also explains how Mesh LLM pools idle compute across devices, why local models and peer-to-peer infrastructure matter, and where he sees the overlap between bitcoin and open source AI. As a longtime open source contributor, Mic closes with advice for anyone looking to get involved in open source projects. title: 21 in 21: Rainey Reitman on Transaction Denied and Financial Censorship
text: Rainey Reitman joins Haley Berkoe on 21 in 21 for a conversation on financial censorship, free speech, and her new book, Transaction Denied: Big Finance’s Power to Punish Speech. Rainey co-founded Freedom of the Press Foundation and serves on the board as president. She also spent 11 years at the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF), first as Activism Director and later as Chief Program Officer. Drawing on years of work in civil liberties advocacy, Rainey explains how lawful speech can still lead to frozen accounts, denied payments, and exclusion from the financial system. She also shares how these issues connect to journalism, whistleblowers, privacy, and Bitcoin’s promise, and limits, as a censorship-resistant tool. *Links to Book:* Amazon: https://a.co/d/04WK0Qek Bookshop: https://bookshop.org/lists/transaction-denied-big-finance-s-power-to-punish-speech Audio: https://www.audible.com/pd/Transaction-Denied-Audiobook/B0FJZRQXXR?source_code=AUDORWS0718179KY7 A portion of every book sale goes to support Freedom of the Press Foundation (https://freedom.press) “In her timely and necessary book, Reitman illuminates the shocking and widespread censorship exerted by the American banking system, details how Orwellian financial surveillance and control has become the norm, and makes a powerful case for why we must push for change if we want to preserve freedom and privacy in the 21st century.” — Alex Gladstein, Chief Strategy Officer, Human Rights Foundation *Follow:* https://x.com/RaineyReitman https://x.com/FreedomofPress *Subscribe:* Apple Podcast: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/21-in-21/id1804684052 Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/show/4UPEsVaAbtQsBtvbKt1RPn?si=331fc0b8368e42b5&nd=1&dlsi=572a5486044e4757

title: 21 in 21: Michael Saylor on Bitcoin, AI, and Advice for Builders
text: Michael Saylor joined Haley Berkoe on 21 in 21 for a rapid-fire conversation on bitcoin, AI, and what’s coming next. He shares what’s top of mind for 2026, why he sees this year as a major turning point, and how he thinks bitcoin could evolve as digital capital beneath new layers of credit and currency. Then, Saylor gets into how AI will radically transform civilization, and how that shift could make bitcoin even more important in a world where autonomous agents need to transact constantly with digital capital. He points to Strategy’s use of AI in creating digital credit products like Stretch (STRC), and shares the kinds of bitcoin products he hopes to see, from deeper integration into everyday technology to applications powered by bitcoin. Saylor emphasizes that we’re entering one of the most fertile periods ever for building, and encourages builders and young people to spend a lot of time learning AI tools and continually pushing themselves to create something new and useful. There are also a few fun detours into MIT prank stories and the AI-generated X profile images he’s become known for. *KEEP WATCHING:* If you enjoyed this conversation, check out our weekly PBJ podcast, where three Presidio Bitcoin members break down what’s happening across bitcoin, AI, and Silicon Valley.

title: Non-Custodial Bitcoin Lending with Surge (Yash Belavadi, Michael Borglin) | Built in the Presidio
text: In the second installment of Built in the Presidio, we sit down with Presidio Bitcoin members Yash Belavadi (Co-founder & CEO) and Michael Borglin (CPO) of Surge, a team building a trust-minimized, non-custodial way to borrow against Bitcoin. We start with why Bitcoin lending keeps reverting to opaque custodians and why these models repeatedly blow up, plus why truly Bitcoin-aligned lending has been so difficult to crack. Then we unpack what’s recently changed - technical primitives, market maturity, and institutional tailwinds - along with Surge's unique approach. Yash and Michael walk through Surge’s high-level architecture, including the role of a distributed custody network, variable vs fixed-rate markets, and what the product feels like for a normal user. We end with the roadmap and core challenges: solving the cold-start liquidity loop while keeping the system verifiable and Bitcoin-native. title: Non-Custodial Bitcoin Lending with Surge (Yash Belavadi, Michael Borglin) | Built in the Presidio
text: In our newest episode of Built in the Presidio, we discuss Surge with CEO Yash Belavadi and Chief Product Officer Michael Borglin. The two Presidio Bitcoin members unpack how Surge is solving one of Bitcoin's most stubborn failure modes: custodial lending. Bitcoin-backed loans are a millenia-old financial idea with a modern upgrade - the use of programmable, verifiable collateral - Bitcoin. Nevertheless, most Bitcoin lending products still require users to hand over their coins to opaque custodians. This has led to a predictable cycle of fast growth during bull markets, followed by large implosions. In this conversation, Yash and Michael cover how they're building a non-custodial lending product that leverages new technical developments along with strategies for bootstrapping liquidity that don't require centralized shortcuts. Other topics covered include: - Why Bitcoin lending keeps drifting back to centralization and custodians - and why those models keep blowing up - Lessons from BlockFi and FTX, and what they changed - The legal and regulatory shifts in how non-custodial protocols can operate - ETF-based lending and what it means for retail - Surge's approach to on-chain risk parameters and distributed custody - Surge user product journey - Challenges around solving the liquidity cold start in a two-sided marketplace Surge embodies Presidio Bitcoin's core ethos: Bitcoin isn't just a financial asset, but a technology that enables better, safer, and more open systems and infrastructure.

title: Presidio Bitcoin Startup Night
text: Presidio Bitcoin Startup Night brought together the PBJ crew and early-stage builders working on bitcoin, self-custodied AI, business treasuries, Lightning-native dollar stability, and bitcoin-backed credit. 0:00 - PBJ intro, format, and checkered investor histories 10:30 - Why Bitcoin startups and VC have not taken off yet 17:47 - Lending, non-custodial gaps, and banks vs. bitcoin startups 24:45 - Developer tools, Nostr stack, and merchant push for bitcoin payments 31:30 - Vora Pitch 42:34 - Castle Pitch 53:17 - Castle Q&A 55:37 - Stable Channels Pitch 1:03:46 - Guarana Bank Pitch Key ideas: - Bitcoin startup investing has lagged because the number of investable companies, venture-scale categories, and mainstream customer use cases has been limited so far. - Exchanges, mining hardware, custody-adjacent products, lending, and holding bitcoin have been the clearest early business models. - The next wave may come from net-new use cases that only bitcoin can enable: global 24/7 payments, self-custodied AI, non-custodial credit, Lightning-native finance, merchant adoption, and Nostr identity. - Developer tools have improved enough that bitcoin applications can now be prototyped quickly with LDK, Lightspark, Lexe-style services, and AI coding tools.

title: Presidio Bitcoin Startup Night
text: - Vora presents self-custodied AI: personal AI hardware secured with user-owned keys, private data, verifiable software, and bitcoin-style recovery. - Castle automates bitcoin treasury allocation for businesses through revenue automation, sweep accounts, treasury thresholds, and integrations with tools such as Stripe, Square, PayPal, Shopify, MindBody, Clover, QuickBooks, and eBay. - Stable Channels proposes self-custodied dollar-denominated balances on Lightning by pairing users who want dollar stability with providers who want leveraged bitcoin exposure. - Guarana Bank presents a shared-custody bitcoin-backed credit app for Latin America, shaped by Argentina's history of currency devaluation and the need to borrow without selling bitcoin or sending collateral to a black-box custodian. text: In this inaugural episode of Built in the Presidio, Vora founders Jesse Posner and Erik Cason discuss the next frontier of self-sovereignty: verifiable hardware and private, self-hosted, user-owned AI. title: BIP 177: Redefining Bitcoin's Base Unit - Mat Balez (Spiral) | Bitcoin Design Week
text: This talk at Presidio Bitcoin Design Week by Mat Balez (Spiral) explores BIP177 and the design challenges of how Bitcoin should be represented in everyday life. From prices at coffee shops to wallet interfaces, the way people see and touch Bitcoin matters. Drawing inspiration from design philosophy (including Johnny Ive’s reflections on care and attention), the session asks: How should Bitcoin quantities be displayed: decimals, sats, or the ₿ symbol? What role do cultural memes and surface areas play in Bitcoin adoption? How can we standardize pricing, wallets, and even keyboards for a Bitcoin future? What happens when the world begins to price everything in Bitcoin? With real-world examples, mockups, and wallet case studies, this track challenges designers to shape Bitcoin’s cultural presence as much as its technical foundations. title: The Design Challenge of Bitcoin Fees - Christoph Ono (Bitcoin Design Foundation) | Design Week
text: This talk at Presidio Bitcoin Design Week explores how fee spikes erode trust, break everyday use cases, and hit hardest in countries where small costs carry huge weight. Through real-world stories and global comparisons, it examines how high fees undermine usability, why UX missteps damage confidence, and what lessons can be drawn from remittances, credit card networks, and existing payment rails. Grounded in the Bitcoin Design Guide, the session asks how better design and communication can make Bitcoin fees understandable, predictable, and fair for users worldwide. title: Bitcoin Design Week 2025: Key Takeaways & Insights
text: Join us inside Bitcoin Design Week 2025 at Presidio Bitcoin in San Francisco. title: Designing Future Payments: Stablecoins vs Bitcoin | Presidio Bitcoin Design Week
text: The future of money is inseparable from the future of payments. Will the next generation of global money apps be built on Bitcoin’s decentralized rails or on stablecoins, dollar-backed tokens with growing regulatory clarity? In this session, Nick Slaney makes the case for Bitcoin as the most accessible, censorship-resistant system for payments, while Daniel Nordh argues for stablecoins as interoperable rails that align with user habits and compliance regimes. The discussion explores the challenges of building a truly global payments app, the role of self-custody, the tradeoffs between stable value and censorship resistance, the UX of on-ramps and off-ramps, and the impact of emerging regulations. title: People Products & Payment Protocols - Conor Okus (Spiral) | Presidio Bitcoin Design Week
text: Bitcoin’s UX is still far from where it needs to be. In this talk, Conor from Spiral reframes the challenge through the lens of people, products, and payment protocols, arguing that design should start with real human needs and work backward to protocol. Drawing from examples like remittances from Los Angeles to Guatemala and freelance payments in Lagos, he highlights how Bitcoin can become both a secure savings tool and a seamless medium for everyday transactions. The session explores design questions around QR codes, payment links, human-readable names, and flexible flows for saving, sending, and spending, laying out a roadmap for building products that make Bitcoin practical for billions. title: Bitchat Grand Design Opportunity - Steve Lee (Spiral) | Presidio Bitcoin Design Week
text: Bitchat is a new peer-to-peer messaging app vibe-coded by Jack Dorsey. It uses Bluetooth mesh networking to let people communicate directly: no servers, no accounts, no centralized control. With its minimalist design, instant onboarding, and ephemeral identities, BitChat has already been adopted in real-world situations like mass protests where privacy and resilience matter. This talk introduces Bitchat’s core principles, from zero-click setup to Nostr-based identity handshakes, explores its design opportunities and challenges, and looks at future possibilities like Bitcoin payments and peer-to-peer exchanges. A glimpse into what communication can look like when it’s local, anonymous, and entirely decentralized. text: Aug 19, 2025 Author of Layered Money and Bitcoin Age, Nik Bhatia (@timevalueofbtc) joined Presidio Bitcoin to share why he watches the 2-year yield over the Fed, how his liquidity index works, what the Eurodollar's shift to stablecoins means for the dollar, and why Bitcoin's growth follows a mathematical power law. title: Handling Quantum-Vulnerable Bitcoins with Jameson Lopp, Hunter Beast, Michael Tidwell & Mike Casey
text: At Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Bitcoin Summit, this panel featuring Jameson Lopp (Casa), Michael Tidwell (ZEBEDEE), Mike Casey (MARA/Anduro), and Hunter Beast (Anduro, Surmount Systems), discussed potential responses to a future where quantum computers can break Bitcoin’s elliptic curve cryptography. The core question was around how to handle quantum-vulnerable coins, particularly pay-to-public-key (P2PK) outputs. Three main strategies were outlined: Do nothing and allow coins to be swept Throttle spending to reduce market disruption (e.g., via Hourglass proposals) Freeze coins to prevent liquidation and preserve economic stability The conversation examined the scope of vulnerable coins, the feasibility of recovery mechanisms, and the implementation of measures like Hourglass V1 and V2. Tradeoffs were explored between security, protocol complexity, user fairness, and Bitcoin’s foundational principles. Other topics included: Legal and social constraints on laundering stolen coins Economic impacts of mass coin movement The role of address reuse and its relation to quantum risk The idea of tail emission and dynamic blockspace adjustment (e.g., “Goldie Blocks”) The risk that fear of quantum attacks may cause more disruption than the attacks themselves The panel closed with a reflection on the difficulty of consensus and the philosophical tension between protecting property rights and preserving network integrity.

title: Quantum-Resistant Rollups with John Light (Alpen Labs) | Quantum Bitcoin Summit
text: In this deep-dive at Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Bitcoin Summit, John Light (Alpen Labs) introduces validity rollups: a powerful scaling technique that can enable high-throughput, post-quantum secure Bitcoin transactions. Starting with the fundamentals of rollup architecture, the talk walks through the distinction between sovereign and smart contract rollups, explains how validity proofs secure asset transfers, and outlines how these rollups can offer trustless bridges, user self-custody, and minimal on-chain data footprints. Light then explores how rollups can be natively quantum-resistant by supporting post-quantum signature schemes and proof systems like STARKs, offering greater scalability and upgrade flexibility than directly modifying Bitcoin Layer 1. The talk concludes with a comparison to other proposals like Shielded CSV and BitZip, and outlines what changes would be needed at the Bitcoin consensus layer—such as OP_CAT, OP_MALL, and disabling keypath spends—to enable quantum-resistant rollups. title: Commit/Reveal with Tadge Dryja (Lightning Network Co-Inventor) | Quantum Bitcoin Summit
text: In this presentation from Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Bitcoin Summit, Tadge Dryja, co-inventor of the Lightning Network, introduces Lifeboat, a lightweight commit/reveal mechanism designed to protect Bitcoin users from short-range quantum attacks, where a quantum adversary learns a public key after it appears in a transaction. Drawing from earlier work like Fawkescoin, Lifeboat enables secure spending without requiring a full post-quantum signature scheme, using a three-hash commitment model (AID, SDP, CTXID) and minimal changes to Bitcoin’s consensus rules. Dryja walks through the threat model, commitment validation process, node storage implications, and attack scenarios. He also discusses deployment challenges, long-term relevance, and how Lifeboat complements future PQ migration strategies. Key themes: quantum resistance, commit/reveal, short-range attacks, soft-fork design, post-quantum Bitcoin security. title: Hourglass with Mike Casey (MARA) | Quantum Bitcoin Summit
text: At Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Bitcoin Summit, Mike Casey (Mara / Anduro) presents Hourglass, a proposal to mitigate quantum theft of vulnerable Bitcoin outputs. Hourglass V1 throttles spending of exposed P2PK coins to 1 per block, stretching liquidation timelines from hours to months. V2 (conceptual) expands this to all revealed public keys, using bloom filters and fee caps to slow mass liquidation and prevent miner collusion. A middle ground between confiscation and theft, preserving optional recovery while buying time in a Q-Day scenario. title: Post-Quantum Signatures and Scaling Bitcoin with STARKs with John Light (Alpen Labs)
text: This talk at Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Bitcoin Summit by John Light (Alpen Labs) presents BitZip, a proposal to mitigate the scalability impact of large post-quantum signatures on Bitcoin’s L1 throughput. BitZip introduces a novel transaction type and a block validity rule that removes all post-quantum signatures from the block and replaces them with a single STARK proof verifying their correctness. title: Hash-Based Signatures with Olaoluwa Osuntokun (Lightning Labs) | Quantum Bitcoin Summit
text: As quantum computing advances, Bitcoin's current digital signatures (ECDSA/Schnorr) face real vulnerabilities. In this technical session, Olaoluwa "Lalu" Osuntokun (Lightning Labs) offers a deep dive into hash-based signature schemes, especially SPHINCS+, as a resilient post-quantum alternative. title: Quantum Threat Modeling with Alex Pruden (Project 11) and Matthew Pines (Bitcoin Policy Institute)
text: While much of Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Bitcoin Summit focused on the “when” of cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs), this final panel shifted focus to the who. Quantum attacks won’t come from hardware alone, they’ll come from adversaries with incentives, cover, and plausible deniability. Drawing from intelligence and military threat modeling, Alex Pruden (CEO of Project 11) and Matthew Pines (Director at Bitcoin Policy Institute) reframed quantum risk as a product of intent × capability × consequence. They outlined three primary adversary profiles: economic, strategic, and ideological, and argued that defenders must begin planning from intent, not just using technical forecasts. title: Post-Quantum Migration with Shai Wyborski | Quantum Bitcoin Summit
text: What happens after a quantum attacker emerges? In this technical talk from Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Bitcoin Summit, researcher Shai Wyborski presents a novel protocol for migrating pre-quantum Bitcoin UTXOs even after the cryptographic break has occurred. Drawing from his research in quantum cryptography, Wyborski explores cryptographic tools that don’t rely on digital signatures. His proposal, built on zero-knowledge proofs, commitment schemes, and modifications to the 2014 “FawkesCoin” construction, offers a modular migration framework. It’s capable of securing “hash,” “derived,” and even some “naked” UTXOs with no trust assumptions or immediate quantum signature deployment. Key themes: Quantum front-running attacks on ECDSA The tradeoffs of freezing vulnerable UTXOs Commit-Delay-Reveal (CDR) cycles and fraud-proof design Post-quantum signature schemes Quantum canaries and on-chain activation triggers Ethical and technical dilemmas of burning lost or stolen coins Wyborski's approach connects academic theory with practical implementation, offering an unconventional but timely path for Bitcoin’s post-quantum security. title: 21 in 21: Pierre Rochard
text: Haley Berkoe sat down with Pierre Rochard, who recently launched The Bitcoin Bond Company. Rochard is a longtime bitcoiner, having previously served as the VP of Research at Riot Platforms and co-founding the Satoshi Nakamoto Institute. HIGHLIGHTS: 2:45 Bitcoin has two fundamental utilities: payments and savings. Cultural tension exists between these use cases. 5:05 It’s challenging for bitcoiners to create products for mainstream users, as we often lack empathy for those who are more risk-averse and not as tech-savvy. 7:48 Institutional adoption serves as an effective educational Trojan horse to disseminate more information about bitcoin’s ethos without diluting the message. 9:27 EMP attack fairlure scenario and the beauty of bitcoin’s decentralization, 11:10 Controversial thoughts around the security budget. 15:09 To positively impact the bitcoin ecosystem, companies can either employ a native bitcoiner or donate to an organization like Brink or OpenSats. 17:52 If Bitcoin replaces the Fed we’ve accomplished the mission but not the whole vision. 18:31 Stablecoins are a stop-gap measure, ideal for individuals outside the US without a dollar bank account. They make it easier to enter bitcoin, serving as a temporary bridge.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Ori as a Telegram bot that can roast you, build apps, make memes, and handle payments, all from your existing group chat

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: The argument that we've already crossed the event horizon. Compute, energy, and intelligence curves going back to Moravec in the 70s and Kurzweil in the 90s suggest singularity isn't just near, it's here.

title: PBJ: Kimi K3 and the Open-Weight Race, AI Treasure Hunting, Bitcoin Falls Further Behind Gold
text: The treasure and Kryptos experiments lead into the singularity tradeoff: spend intelligence solving human puzzles now, or spend it recursively improving the next generation of models. The hosts answer the existential uncertainty partly with a practical ethic—do worthwhile work with people you value in the present.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: Jack Dorsey's claim that data provenance, protocols, evals, and weights now matter more than open source code becomes a framework for AI transparency. The hosts focus on proving training inputs, who submitted them, and when a model was created, with Nostr keys and OpenTimestamps floated as a bitcoin-native provenance layer.

title: 21 in 21: Patrick Ball on Using Bitcoin and AI to Defend Human Rights
text: To keep future human-rights evidence from being dismissed as AI slop, HRDAG signs and hashes its data and anchors Merkle roots through OpenTimestamps so it can prove the material existed by a specific Bitcoin block.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: Anthropic's rumored Mythos model and the apparent nerfing of public Claude frame a strategic risk for companies building around one frontier provider. If the best model is reserved for governments, banks, or premium tiers, model dependency can become an existential switching-cost problem.

title: PBJ: Saylor to sell bitcoin, Block smashes earnings, Anthropic to overtake Google w xAI
text: Anthropic is framed as a beast of an enterprise AI company whose demand may have outgrown its compute supply. The hosts discuss Amazon and Google compute deals, Claude throttling, and whether Anthropic could become more valuable than Google.

title: PBJ: Anthropic's Fable Drama, Personhood for AI, Bark Launches on Mainnet
text: Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos drama becomes a test case for frontier-model release policy. The hosts weigh restricted access for zero-day discovery against the reality that powerful capabilities will diffuse and be distilled quickly.

title: PBJ: New Open USD Stablecoin, Fable 5 is Back, Open Source AI with Goose & Buzz
text: Max describes getting Claude-pilled and then noticing Claude becoming more paternalistic, while wondering whether the returned Fable model is the same capability people saw before the restriction drama.

title: PBJ: Announcing PB's Open Source AI Summit, Bitcoin Forks, Local AI Builder Recap
text: The Fable 5 export-control story is treated as a watershed AI governance moment: if foreign nationals, even inside the United States or inside Anthropic, cannot use a model, release policy and research access start looking like national-security infrastructure.

title: Unpacking Bitcoin's Underperformance, Vibecoding with Nostr, Prediction Markets
text: The thesis from a Type One Summit speaker that bitcoin functions as a thermodynamic system uniquely suited for AI agents to use as collateral. Bitcoin's permissionless nature makes it the default monetary infrastructure for autonomous AI, which traditional financial systems would never allow access to.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: The original bitcoin-as-everyday-money use case from the whitepaper is being revived. Eight years of digital gold narrative dominance may be ending as technical and UX barriers to spending are solved by AI payments and merchant adoption.

title: Bitcoin's Branding Problem, AI's Impact on Open Source, Can Spiral's Playbook Work for AI?
text: Bitcoin as everyday money is defended against the objection that no one wants to spend an appreciating asset. The hosts flip the framing to the seller side: if bitcoin is the better money, merchants may eventually prefer receiving it and offer incentives that pull buyers into the monetary transition.

title: Why Silicon Valley Misses Bitcoin, Corporate Adoption (Block vs Stripe), New Builder Tools
text: Bitcoin as everyday money is discussed through the practical objection that people do not want to spend an appreciating asset. The hosts answer with spend-and-replace, tax friction, and interoperable dollars over bitcoin or Lightning, separating bitcoin the asset from bitcoin the payment network.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: Cash App, BitKey, and other major bitcoin products switched UI from showing sats to the ₿ symbol. A concrete step toward making bitcoin legible to non-technical merchants and consumers.

title: BIP 177: Redefining Bitcoin's Base Unit - Mat Balez (Spiral) | Bitcoin Design Week
text: Mat argues that prices and wallet balances should use the ₿ symbol and integer-style display so bitcoin's cultural surface area remains bitcoin, not an obscure unit label users have to decode.

title: Our 2026 Predictions, Contentious Forks, Vibe Coding Community
text: Steve's lone new prediction is that the Bitcoin ₿ symbol becomes the dominant consumer unit marker in 2026. The idea is that UI standardization can make bitcoin feel less like a technical asset and more like ordinary money.

title: Defining bitcoin spam, is MSTR the next bubble, $20 million Coinbase ransom
text: Bitcoin units are revisited through the idea of rebasing away from sats toward a simpler consumer denomination. The segment matters because the hosts see unit language as a coordination problem that could change quickly if major apps like Cash App and Coinbase move together.

title: Unpacking Bitcoin's Underperformance, Vibecoding with Nostr, Prediction Markets
text: The case for a collateralized bitcoin lending product that lets holders gain exposure to major AI companies (Google, Anthropic, xAI) without selling their BTC. Deposit bitcoin as collateral, invest in AI equity upside, stay long bitcoin. Described as a product that will 'absolutely print' once regulatory clarity arrives.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: Coinbase's mortgage product is framed as a new form of bitcoin-backed lending: roughly 40% LTV, no margin calls if BTC drops, and a practical down-payment path for holders who do not want to sell. The deeper signal is traditional mortgage infrastructure, including Fannie Mae-style conforming loans, beginning to treat bitcoin as credible collateral.

title: PBJ: Frontier Models Eating All, SF's AI Dominance, What Happened at Bitcoin Vegas
text: The lending segment revisits the core borrower problem: access liquidity without selling bitcoin, while avoiding opaque custody, rehypothecation, and brittle liquidation mechanics. The hosts compare strategies rather than assuming every bitcoin loan is the same product.

title: Presidio Bitcoin Startup Night
text: Bitcoin lending is presented as one of the business models with clear product-market fit because holders want liquidity without selling and triggering taxes. The unresolved challenge is whether lenders can avoid opaque custody and rehypothecation risk.

title: Non-Custodial Bitcoin Lending with Surge (Yash Belavadi, Michael Borglin) | Built in the Presidio
text: The Surge episode opens by framing bitcoin lending as an old financial market with a uniquely bitcoin failure mode: repeated cycles of lending growth followed by collapses when custody and trust are handled poorly.

title: Strikes new bitcoin loan product, Knots taking market share, Nostr: blossoms & Noauth
text: Strike's loan product is evaluated alongside Lava and Coinbase as part of the emerging bitcoin-collateralized lending market. The hosts care less about the announcement itself than whether users can borrow dollars against BTC without selling or accepting opaque custody risk.

title: Bitchat's growing adoption, Future of stablecoins, Bitcoin lending
text: Bitcoin lending is treated through Lava's actual user behavior: deposit BTC, borrow stablecoin dollars, then sometimes use the proceeds to buy more bitcoin. The hosts separate legitimate dollar liquidity from circular leverage, asking whether the UI should model risks and guide users rather than blindly encourage the behavior.

title: PBJ: USDC on Cash App, Wand Launch, Surge, and the Zcash Crash
text: The Surge launch revisits the core borrower job: access dollars without selling bitcoin, while avoiding opaque custody and rehypothecation. The product is framed as a line of credit rather than a conventional term loan.

title: PBJ: USDC on Cash App, Wand Launch, Surge, and the Zcash Crash
text: The hosts identify a large product opportunity: let bitcoin holders post BTC and buy exposure to AI companies like Google, Anthropic, xAI, OpenAI, or Nvidia without selling their bitcoin. The winning version would make that collateralized flow easy and ideally non-custodial.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: The worst-case quantum scenario is framed as ugly but survivable: most exposed value could move quickly if there is warning, while an extreme real-time break would force debate over freezing, reorgs, or emergency signature upgrades. The 2018 inflation bug is used as precedent that Core, pools, and exchanges can coordinate rapidly when they must.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: Merchants are turning on bitcoin payments, then being told to turn them off by their accountants due to tax confusion. A tax specialist published guidance clarifying that immediately converting to fiat has no tax consequences, removing a key barrier.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: Square's default bitcoin payments rollout is a material step, but the hosts map the remaining adoption friction: hardware and software rollout gaps, sellers who do not know the feature exists, unified QR expectations, tipping flows, and the need to message Cash App payments as a fee-saving merchant benefit.

title: Presidio Bitcoin Startup Night
text: Square's bitcoin payments launch becomes the prompt for a practical merchant push. Spiral's materials focus on the merchant-facing benefit of saving payment fees, because that message lands before ideological arguments about censorship resistance or privacy.

title: 21 in 21: Rod Roudi on Bitcoin Park, Events, and Merchant Adoption
text: Rod focuses on reducing merchant friction as the key to getting more businesses to accept bitcoin, drawing from Bitcoin Park's experience and the business side of payments.

title: 21 in 21: Joe Carlo on How Bitcoin Changed Pink Owl Coffee Forever
text: Joe Carlo explains Pink Owl Coffee's move into accepting bitcoin through Square, showing merchant adoption as an operating decision rather than a slogan.

title: Bitcoin at the Register: Inspiring Merchants - Haley Berkoe (Spiral) | Presidio Bitcoin Design Week
text: Haley Berkoe frames merchant adoption as a design and storytelling challenge: bitcoin has to move beyond digital gold and become easy, fun, and rewarding at the register.

title: Bitcoin's Branding Problem, AI's Impact on Open Source, Can Spiral's Playbook Work for AI?
text: Square's broader bitcoin payments rollout is a real adoption win, but not the finish line. Sellers still need awareness, Bitcoin Map opt-in, customer-facing promotion, a cleaner unified QR flow, and UI that makes zero-fee bitcoin payments obvious enough to change merchant behavior.

title: Bitcoin Acceptance on Square, Unpacking the Lava Drama, CashApp & Lightning Dollars
text: Square's bitcoin acceptance going GA turns merchant adoption from announcement into operational reality. The hosts map the real rollout details: a few taps for many sellers, gotchas around upgrades and configuration, and the need to explain why lower payment fees can materially improve margins.

title: PBJ : Strike's BTC-backed credit line, Zcash if Bitcoin fails, Merchant adoption with Square
text: Merchant adoption is framed in margin language rather than ideology: cutting processing fees from 3% to 1% can be a dramatic profit improvement for low-margin businesses. The hosts argue for simple leave-behind materials that help employees and owners understand the pitch after the conversation ends.

title: Square's big release, Insatiable energy demand, Update from Berlin Conference
text: Square's release is framed as both a product rollout and a normalization strategy: Bitcoin stickers in stores make the payment option feel real, while merchant BTC conversions let sellers route a percentage of fiat sales into bitcoin automatically. Acceptance going live for all merchants, paired with waived fees, creates a practical adoption path rather than just another announcement.

title: Reflections from Vegas, Generating 10% Lightning yield, Circle IPO
text: The Vegas recap grounds merchant adoption in messy real-world payment attempts: Square terminal bitcoin payments worked, but venue internet, store rollout gaps, and staff awareness still mattered. The takeaway is that payment availability is only one layer of adoption; operational reliability and merchant education decide whether users experience it as real.

title: PBJ: Saylor to sell bitcoin, Block smashes earnings, Anthropic to overtake Google w xAI
text: Cafe RX shows merchant adoption moving from friction to excitement once bitcoin payments are a default option and regular customers use them. The hosts emphasize that usage, tips, and visible customer enthusiasm can turn a skeptical merchant into a promoter.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: Presidio Bitcoin's quantum readiness report is presented as a neutral, investor-friendly public good rather than a one-off PDF. It is designed as a living GitHub project that maps the threat, current work, and response paths across short, medium, long, and never-happens timelines.

title: Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report
text: The report frames bitcoin quantum readiness as a living map of exposure, mitigations, and upgrade paths, with practical hygiene now and staged protocol work if credible CRQC signals strengthen.

title: Unveiling Flint, Michael Saylor on What Bitcoin Did, Comparing Bitcoin Treasuries
text: MicroStrategy and Metaplanet aren't competitors. Different leverage strategies and different markets (US vs Japan) create space for multiple winners rather than winner-take-all dynamics. All bitcoin accumulation by public companies serves the shared goal regardless of strategy differences.

title: Unpacking Bitchat, MSTR Earnings, In-kind bitcoin ETF approval
text: Bitcoin treasury companies are examined as a possible adoption risk when too much demand flows through companies and ETFs rather than direct use. The hosts ask whether treasury-company success can strengthen bitcoin financially while weakening payment demand, self-custody, and block-space usage.

title: Life on a bitcoin standard, version control for vibe coding, BTC treasury company saturation
text: Bitcoin treasury company saturation becomes a community topic rather than only a market topic. The hosts propose a recurring meetup to track strategies, risks, and global expansion as the category spreads beyond early public-company pioneers.

title: Defining bitcoin spam, is MSTR the next bubble, $20 million Coinbase ransom
text: Bitcoin treasury companies are debated as the category spreads beyond Strategy and XXI. The hosts contrast aggressive levered bitcoin plays with the more conservative Block-style approach of holding a single-digit percentage of corporate treasury in BTC.

title: The Bitcoin Age with Nik Bhatia
text: Nik reads bitcoin treasury companies through network growth: as bitcoin matures, corporate adoption is a natural stage. He expects Strategy to keep issuing capital and acquiring bitcoin, while avoiding security-level calls on MSTR's capital structure.

title: The Bitcoin Age with Nik Bhatia
text: Nik warns that some treasury companies may botch the financial engineering, creating volatility, forced sellers, or liquidation cascades. His answer is to watch market behavior and price action rather than underwrite every balance sheet.

title: PBJ: Saylor to sell bitcoin, Block smashes earnings, Anthropic to overtake Google w xAI
text: Block's bitcoin treasury policy is compared with Strategy and Coinbase: Block buys bitcoin through a recurring percentage of bitcoin-related gross profit, which is less dramatic than MSTR-style issuance but still makes BTC a standing treasury practice.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: Bitcoin's underperformance attributed to crypto contagion and the 'digital gold' narrative losing to actual gold (which ran from $3k to $5.4k on central bank buying). Central banks lack the operational infrastructure for bitcoin that they have for gold, so the comparison isn't apples-to-apples.

title: Signal using Bitcoin, Funding development, Perspectives of Jack, Saylor & Elon
text: Central banks have institutional custody processes for gold but not bitcoin, which the hosts argue explains why gold is outperforming during the current macro crisis. They call this probably the last cycle where that dynamic holds, as sovereign bitcoin custody infrastructure slowly catches up.

title: Type 1 Energy Summit, The Billionaire Flippening, and iPhone 17’s Memory Upgrade
text: Gold's renewed strength becomes a way to revisit bitcoin's digital-gold narrative. The hosts argue that tech people often need to understand why gold matters before bitcoin's monetary upgrade story makes sense.

title: The Bitcoin Age with Nik Bhatia
text: Nik contrasts gold's larger market cap with bitcoin's stronger momentum. Gold remains the older reserve asset, but bitcoin is the one rallying people around a new neutral collateral and settlement thesis.

title: PBJ: Kimi K3 and the Open-Weight Race, AI Treasure Hunting, Bitcoin Falls Further Behind Gold
text: Steve revisits bitcoin priced in gold rather than nominal dollars and finds the ratio dramatically worse than a year earlier—roughly halved, and at one point closer to one-third of the prior level. He argues bitcoiners should track this comparison alongside the unadjusted dollar price rather than selecting only the most flattering denominator.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: Jack Dorsey and Roelof Botha's 'hierarchy to intelligence' frame points to Block reorganizing around agents rather than managers as information routers. Builder Bot is the concrete example: a Slack-integrated company world model that can answer questions, surface SQL, point to internal experts, and reduce meeting friction.

title: Meta Stablecoins Return, Open-Source Agents, OpenClaw Builder Meetup
text: Block's 40% layoff is framed as AI-driven restructuring rather than financial distress, with Spiral spared and Cash App still growing gross profit. The discussion combines the human cost with the broader adaptation thesis: companies will get leaner, and displaced workers may need entrepreneurial paths such as vibe-coding workshops and MDK-style ways to build and earn online.

title: Did Quantum FUD Price, Bitcoin Merchant Community, Competing with  Stripe
text: Block Investor Day is read as a test of whether mainstream investors understand Block's bitcoin strategy. The segment focuses on how bitcoin payments, Square merchants, and Cash App fit into a long-term platform story that may not map neatly to quarterly expectations.

title: Amjad & Paul Graham notice MDK, What is BuckToken, Walmart sorta accepts Bitcoin
text: Travis Vander Zanden's BUCK token is a stablecoin built on top of MicroStrategy's Stretch instrument. Stretch over-collateralizes bitcoin to yield ~11%, and Buck passes 7% to users while keeping a ~4% spread. Unavailable to US users due to stablecoin yield-sharing regulations. The hosts see it as the first live manifestation of Saylor's capital-to-credit-to-money stack.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Cash App dollars on Lightning as the template for mass adoption without asking anyone to become a bitcoiner first

title: PBJ: Frontier Models Eating All, SF's AI Dominance, What Happened at Bitcoin Vegas
text: Cash App's 5% bitcoin-back offer and P2P bitcoin payments are treated as mainstream distribution moments. The hosts focus on rewards and familiar peer payments as ways to normalize bitcoin without requiring users to start from ideology.

title: Cash App Brand Design & Lessons for Branding Bitcoin - Kyle Fletcher (Block) | Bitcoin Design Week
text: Kyle uses Cash App's bitcoin-facing brand work as a case study in making bitcoin feel approachable, useful, and culturally legible without forcing every user through technical explanations first.

title: Bitcoin Acceptance on Square, Unpacking the Lava Drama, CashApp & Lightning Dollars
text: Cash App's dollars-over-Lightning path is treated as a potentially historic product shift: a user can hold dollars, send through Cash App, and have the recipient receive bitcoin over Lightning. The hosts frame it as a remittance and payment-network threat because it makes bitcoin rails invisible to the sender.

title: PBJ: Saylor to sell bitcoin, Block smashes earnings, Anthropic to overtake Google w xAI
text: Cash App's 5% back in bitcoin at Square terminals is treated as a powerful adoption wedge: a user can pay dollars over Lightning, receive bitcoin rewards, and suddenly have a reason to prefer Cash App over credit cards.

title: PBJ: USDC on Cash App, Wand Launch, Surge, and the Zcash Crash
text: Cash App's Wand extends the payment surface beyond phones and cards into a small passive NFC object, suggesting Cash App can keep experimenting with form factor, youth culture, and bitcoin rewards without making the product feel like crypto.

title: PBJ: USDC on Cash App, Wand Launch, Surge, and the Zcash Crash
text: Cash App's USDC integration is praised because stablecoin deposits appear inside the ordinary dollar balance. Users do not have to manage separate stablecoin and bank-dollar buckets, which makes the crypto rail disappear into familiar money UX.

title: Unveiling Flint, Michael Saylor on What Bitcoin Did, Comparing Bitcoin Treasuries
text: Spiral launches Flint (flints.dev), a curated community for AI-assisted developers with three tiers: Kindling (early apps), Firewood (published apps), and Blaze (commercialized products). The goal is to be a tastemaker destination that surfaces quality work as vibe-coded apps proliferate and discovery becomes the hard problem.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: Flint's private idea channel becomes a template for public, crowdfunded vibe coding: anyone could propose an app, have humans and bots debate the architecture, and fund the build with bitcoin. The point is turning community taste and AI implementation into a repeatable software-production loop.

title: Unpacking Bitcoin's Underperformance, Vibecoding with Nostr, Prediction Markets
text: Christopher David at Open Agents is building a bitcoin-powered GPU marketplace where owners of spare Apple Silicon can plug in and earn sats. Key called it 'fracking for Apple M chips.' The hosts see bitcoin as the natural economic coordination layer: when economics (not privacy) drives hybrid cloud/local AI infrastructure, open permissionless payments win by default.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: Open Agents, Owls, Sprout, and Block's Mesh-LLM all point toward open networks for training and serving AI with spare compute. The hosts frame bitcoin and sats as the natural payout layer, but emphasize that demand generation and verifiable execution are the next hard problems.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Ori 10x's both casual AI use and solo vibe coding. Software emerges from the conversation you're already having, not from going to an IDE with a spec. Super Bowl betting pool as an example.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: Google's paper linking quantum computing to AI acceleration caught the hosts off guard because they had not seen AI treated as a known quantum application. If quantum unlocks new AI capabilities, the resulting investment could increase the probability of viable quantum computers and compress the timeline.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: Google's quantum paper claims a 20x improvement in the algorithmic path to breaking elliptic-curve cryptography, with a zero-knowledge proof that the details exist without revealing them. Steve frames it as 'n minus one': material progress, but not proof that bitcoin breakage is imminent.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: Reports that Iran was charging ships a Strait of Hormuz toll in bitcoin are treated as a major geopolitical use case, even with the facts still uncertain. The segment highlights bitcoin's liquidity, sanctions resistance, and the unusual pattern of a dollar-denominated fee settled in bitcoin.

title: Amjad & Paul Graham notice MDK, What is BuckToken, Walmart sorta accepts Bitcoin
text: Jack Dorsey visited Presidio Bitcoin for an off-the-record AMA with about 20 members. The most candid he'd been publicly, with frank answers to questions that wouldn't get asked on a Block investor day.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: Lexe's launch is treated as a serious Lightning UX breakthrough: each user gets an LDK node in the cloud inside Intel SGX, while the wallet provider does not hold the private keys. The trade-off aims to preserve self-custody while solving offline receiving, persistent connectivity, and multi-device wallet access.

title: Member Spotlight: Lexe (Max Fang & Philip Hayes)
text: Max Fang and Philip Hayes describe Lexe as Lightning infrastructure that runs user nodes inside cloud hardware enclaves, aiming for a custodial-feeling Lightning experience while keeping the wallet self-custodial.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Voltage facilitated a $1M payment between Secure Digital Markets (SDM) and Kraken over Lightning in under a second. Direct channel with no routing, but a clear signal that the network has matured.

title: Meta Stablecoins Return, Open-Source Agents, OpenClaw Builder Meetup
text: Lightning usage is measured through imperfect but improving volume estimates: River reports roughly $1 billion per month and more than 5 million payments, despite the network's private routing design. The key signal is that settlement volume appears to be compounding while most attention is elsewhere.

title: PBJ: Bitcoin Core v31 Release, Project Loupe Launches, Lightning Network's Future
text: Steve contrasts LDK Server with other Lightning stacks by pointing to LDK's feature lead: splicing, BOLT 12, async payments, and lower-level customizability. The argument is that Lightning infrastructure should be easier to run without giving up protocol-level power.

title: Unpacking Bitcoin's Underperformance, Vibecoding with Nostr, Prediction Markets
text: A Nostr-native meme marketplace where creators earn bitcoin through zaps. The vision includes revenue waterfalls where sharers earn a cut when their shared content gets zapped downstream, creating viral economic incentives.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: Mesh-LLM is described as Block's early peer-to-peer GPU network: useful as a community compute layer today, but not yet a marketplace. The roadmap questions are payments and proofs: how nodes get paid, and how users know the expected model actually ran.

title: PBJ: Frontier Models Eating All, SF's AI Dominance, What Happened at Bitcoin Vegas
text: Builder's Mesh-LLM presentation is described as a practical peer-to-peer compute experiment: pool spare machines, distribute open-model workloads, and make AI inference feel more like a network than a centralized cloud account.

title: Goose Developers on the Future of Open-Source AI Agents
text: Mesh-LLM is presented as a peer-to-peer inference project that grew out of Goose's local-model work, combining heterogeneous machines to make open-weight intelligence more available.

title: PBJ: Goose Development Kit, Spiral Expands Into AI, Can Bitcoin Names Scale?
text: PBJ checks in on Mesh-LLM after the Goose retreat, with Steve noting that contributors beyond Mick are now spending serious time on it and that the project is moving from experiment toward a more substantial shared-compute layer.

title: 21 in 21: Mic Neale on goose, Mesh LLM, and Open Source AI
text: Mesh-LLM pools heterogeneous devices—from laptops and gaming rigs to racks—so models can check one another or split layers across machines, using idle compute that no single device could turn into capable inference alone.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: A Reddit-like social network that emerged for AI bots to interact with each other, requiring Twitter verification that you're a bot. Part performance art, but an early real-world indicator of AI agents building their own communities and communication layer.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: Origin story of what became OpenClaw. Started as ClawdBot (a riff on Claude), went viral, rebranded to MoltBot, then OpenClaw, all within a week. The two rebrands didn't kill momentum because the core product-market fit (AI agent via Telegram on your local machine) was undeniable.

title: Unveiling Flint, Michael Saylor on What Bitcoin Did, Comparing Bitcoin Treasuries
text: Saylor's intellectual framework: Will Durant's 11-volume world history and Rothbard's economic histories as foundation. Every civilization has had its '1971 moment.' Currency debasement is the oldest trick, not something new. History rhymes in a spiral, not a circle. Bitcoin as the pristine collateral that breaks the cycle. Max recommends his What Bitcoin Did appearance for the depth of his reading list alone.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Ori is built by the MDK team. Bitcoin payments are a core competency but deliberately not front-and-center in the pitch, and why frictionless payments transform group chat experiences like prediction markets and trivia.

title: Amjad & Paul Graham notice MDK, What is BuckToken, Walmart sorta accepts Bitcoin
text: Replit's CEO Amjad and then Paul Graham both publicly endorsed MDK after Nick framed it as 'permissionless global payments' rather than 'bitcoin payments.' The hosts see this as the template for getting bitcoin mainstream: position as enabling infrastructure, not as a technology choice.

title: 21 in 21, a Rapid-Fire Bitcoin Q&A Podcast: Nick Slaney
text: Nick Slaney introduces Money Dev Kit, a startup building tools that make it easier for developers to add bitcoin and Lightning payments to applications.

title: 21 in 21, a Rapid-Fire Bitcoin Q&A Podcast: Nick Slaney
text: Nick Slaney introduces Money Dev Kit as a startup making it easier for developers to add bitcoin and Lightning payments to applications without becoming payment-infrastructure experts.

title: Did Quantum FUD Price, Bitcoin Merchant Community, Competing with  Stripe
text: MDK's Stripe comparison is about developer experience, not only speed: five-minute payment setup may become table stakes across Spark, Lexe, and other SDKs. The differentiator is messaging, docs, support, and a product surface that lets vibe coders add payments without understanding APIs or pull requests.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: The case for Nostr as natural infrastructure for autonomous AI agents. Public/private key pairs as identity require no centralized accounts, JB55 already has a bot live on Nostr, and bots are already zapping bitcoin to each other autonomously.

title: Unveiling Flint, Michael Saylor on What Bitcoin Did, Comparing Bitcoin Treasuries
text: In a world of infinite vibe-coded apps, identity and social graph infrastructure becomes the critical differentiator. Nostr offers an open alternative to Google/Apple login, and open leaderboards, friend networks, and Zap-based discovery signals create network effects without requiring custom backend infrastructure per app.

title: Vibe coding nostr, open source bounties, Phoenix rises from the ashes
text: Nostr is framed as the missing global identity and data commons for AI-built apps. Existing services may keep extending their data moats, but new agentic apps need portable identity, open payments, and shared data primitives that Nostr already points toward.

title: Vibe coding with bitcoin and Nostr, Balaji on China, and off-grid mining
text: Vibe coding with bitcoin and Nostr is framed as the open alternative to defaulting to Google auth, X identity, and Stripe payments. The opportunity is a plug-and-play app environment where builders can choose Nostr identity and bitcoin payments as first-class modules.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Recap of the first OpenClaw meetup at Presidio Bitcoin. 10-12 members got it running and why it matters.

title: Moltbot is Molting Again, Musk SpaceX and xAI Merger, Is Crypto Dying
text: Origin story: went viral as ClawdBot, rebranded twice in a week to MoltBot then OpenClaw. Full OS-level computer control via Telegram, fastest to 100k GitHub stars.

title: Meta Stablecoins Return, Open-Source Agents, OpenClaw Builder Meetup
text: The OpenClaw Builder Meetup becomes a signal that local, agentic tooling has crossed from curiosity into community infrastructure. The index itself is mentioned as a way to find OpenClaw segments across episodes, reinforcing how quickly the topic became recurring.

title: OpenClaw joins OpenAI, Agent Wallets and Payments, Lightning v Stablecoins for Agentic Commerce
text: OpenClaw's skill and tool ecosystem is framed as something likely to trend open source because the components are cheap for agents to recreate once the pattern is visible. The durable value may shift from individual tools to hubs, workflows, and agent collaboration surfaces.

title: OpenClaw joins OpenAI, Agent Wallets and Payments, Lightning v Stablecoins for Agentic Commerce
text: The 'OpenClaw joins OpenAI' segment treats the acquisition-or-alignment story as both plausible product evolution and a source of suspicion. The sharper question is whether OpenClaw's unsafe, local-control aesthetic was organically popular or strategically useful to OpenAI in the frontier-model narrative fight.

title: 21 in 21: Calle on Cashu, Clawi, and AI Agents
text: Calle places OpenClaw in a third chapter of AI usage: always-online personal agents that can keep working through Telegram or other messaging surfaces even when the user is not actively babysitting a browser chat.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Ori as a productized OpenClaw under the hood. Add it to your Telegram group and it integrates natively, with the transition from OpenClaw as a raw tool to Ori as something ready for everyday group use.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: OpenAI's acquisition of TBPN is treated as a media and distribution move, not just a content deal. The strategic logic is that OpenAI needs its own high-value tech audience channel while Anthropic dominates daily mindshare and competitors buy visibility through ads.

title: OpenAI and Worldcoin, PB Hackathon Highlights, and Kraken’s xStocks
text: OpenAI's acquisition of Jony Ive's company is interpreted as a hardware and interface bet. The discussion frames it as OpenAI trying to own the next consumer AI surface, not just the model layer.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: Agentic payments expose a privacy gap in public-chain stablecoin rails: paying someone on Base can reveal a wallet balance and transaction history to the recipient or the internet. The hosts contrast that with normal user expectations, Lightning's better privacy properties, and Tempo's promised compliance-friendly shielded privacy.

title: Amjad & Paul Graham notice MDK, What is BuckToken, Walmart sorta accepts Bitcoin
text: Prediction markets as information discovery infrastructure, not gambling. Stacker News demonstrates the principle: Bitcoin-paid upvotes create non-forgeable signal that bots can't fabricate. AI agents with wallets competing in markets produces emergent intelligence that beats central planning.

title: Unpacking Bitcoin's Underperformance, Vibecoding with Nostr, Prediction Markets
text: Enormous pricing gaps between Polymarket and Kalshi on the same outcomes create obvious arbitrage that should be closing but isn't. AI tools could exploit these gaps and build permissionless access for users excluded from US prediction markets.

title: Presidio Bitcoin Startup Night
text: Prediction markets are discussed as a native form of bitcoin-enabled gaming. Nostr and bitcoin can combine publishing and payments in a way that may open designs that are difficult under conventional regulatory and payment infrastructure.

title: Bitcoin in AI Models, Fold's Gift Cards, Bitkey Private Purchasing
text: Prediction markets going mainstream prompts a distinction between gambling and investing at the tails. The hosts treat the category as culturally important because it changes how people price uncertainty, risk, and conviction in public.

title: 17 Years Since the White Paper, BIP 444 Fork Announced, Square v Saylors Bitcoin Approach
text: Prediction markets are revisited through Polymarket accepting bitcoin and Predyx offering a bitcoin-native experience. Predyx's LNURL login, no-email onboarding, and instant Lightning deposits show how bitcoin identity and payments can make market UX feel unusually lightweight.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: A prototype quantum-safe bitcoin transaction can be done today without consensus changes, but the trade-offs are severe. It relies on brute-forcing hash values, may cost around $150 per key, and creates a non-standard transaction that likely needs a direct miner path such as Slipstream.

title: Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report
text: The report includes QSB as a no-consensus-change experiment that can demonstrate quantum-safe transaction construction today, while making the cost and relay trade-offs explicit.

title: Unpacking Bitcoin's Underperformance, Vibecoding with Nostr, Prediction Markets
text: MDK did the hard polish work to make bitcoin payments first-class in Replit. Now someone needs to do the same for Nostr. Alex Gleason's Shakespeare is a Nostr-native alternative, but Replit has the user base, so the higher-leverage move is integrating Nostr as a first-class citizen there. The template: do the hard work once, and everyone can build on top of it.

title: Vibe coding nostr, open source bounties, Phoenix rises from the ashes
text: The hosts sketch a Replit-on-open-protocols vision: Nostr for identity, Bitcoin Lightning for payments, and native secret management built into the dev environment. Karpathy's public frustration with vibe-coding credential sprawl is the prompt, and the pitch is that open infrastructure solves what closed platforms cannot.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Prompt injection, malware as a top OpenClaw add-on, 'just assume everything on your local machine is already leaked.' Plus the notification overload problem and whether this all goes Black Mirror faster than we think.

title: 21 in 21: Mic Neale on goose, Mesh LLM, and Open Source AI
text: Rather than treating repeated permission prompts as the safety boundary, Goose assumes users may approve requests without reading them and makes safe autonomous behavior a responsibility of the harness itself.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: The naming project is reframed from human self-sovereign names into agent-based network resources. In an agent-first internet, humans still need speakable, memorable names that map to cryptographic keys without depending on DNS gatekeepers like registrars, ICANN, or Cloudflare.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: Blockstream's SHRINCS and SHRIMPS are compared as complementary post-quantum signature schemes. SHRINCS gets close to practical size at roughly five times today's Schnorr signature but requires retained state, while SHRIMPS is larger and stateless, making it better suited to recovery paths.

title: Human Bitcoin Addresses, SHRINCS Post-Quantum Signatures, Bitcoin Gift Cards
text: SHRINCS and related hash-based signature work are introduced as a practical path toward quantum-resistant bitcoin signatures. The credibility of the authors matters because the proposal sits in the uncomfortable middle ground between real research progress and quantum-risk panic.

title: Y Combinator's USDC Move, Ori Agent Group Chats, OpenClaw Meetup
text: Skepticism on YC telling startups to use USDC. The 'intranet on intranets' critique of stablecoin platforms vs. open bitcoin/Lightning rails.

title: Bitcoin Acceptance on Square, Unpacking the Lava Drama, CashApp & Lightning Dollars
text: Stablecoins are compared with Cash App's dollar-over-Lightning path: both can hide volatile BTC from users, but Lightning keeps the settlement network bitcoin-native. The hosts use the comparison to ask whether stablecoins and Lightning compete or converge in consumer payment UX.

title: PBJ: USDC on Cash App, Wand Launch, Surge, and the Zcash Crash
text: Cash App's USDC rollout is framed as the best stablecoin UX the hosts have seen because USDC simply shows up as dollars. The deeper product point is that stablecoins become more useful when users do not have to think about which dollar rail they are using.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: Stretch-backed stablecoins are pitched as a regional fintech opportunity: exchanges or licensed settlement companies outside the US could offer dollar savings products backed by bitcoin credit rather than waiting for American regulatory clarity. The main constraint is distribution and interoperability, since new stablecoin issuers still need wallets, Stripe-like bridges, and local payment networks to accept them.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: The Sovereign Individual thesis is reframed for AI: cryptography and bitcoin shifted power toward individuals, while frontier AI may re-centralize power into a few model companies. The open question is whether open models at the edge can preserve the individual-sovereignty arc.

title: Presidio Bitcoin launches, Crypto Summit/SBR, Renewable Energy Bitcoin Mining, and more...
text: The Sovereign Individual is revisited through US state adoption and the possibility that bitcoin changes the balance between individuals, companies, and governments. The early PBJ framing already treats bitcoin as political technology, not only an investment.

title: Unveiling Flint, Michael Saylor on What Bitcoin Did, Comparing Bitcoin Treasuries
text: MicroStrategy's Stretch instrument over-collateralizes bitcoin 6x to offer ~11% yields versus 3-4% from traditional bonds. The only belief required: Bitcoin won't drop 85-90% over the bond term. Max sees Stretch as the bridge between old-world capital mandates and bitcoin collateral, without requiring self-custody.

title: Presidio Bitcoin's Quantum Readiness Report, Iran Wants Bitcoin, Can Mythos Break Bitcoin?
text: Taproot's cheapest key-spend path exposes a public key, which is the core quantum concern. The discussion covers future soft-fork designs that could disable vulnerable key spends while preserving script paths, plus BIP 360 as a Taproot-like output type meant to support quantum signatures.

title: PBJ: USDC on Cash App, Wand Launch, Surge, and the Zcash Crash
text: Surge is used as a practical Taproot use case: multiple spending scripts can exist behind a single bitcoin output, and only the path actually used needs to be revealed. That privacy and flexibility matter for non-custodial lending design.

title: Google's Quantum Warning Overblown?, OpenAI Acquires TBPN, Jack Dorsey Makes Block Mini-AGI
text: Verifiable compute is identified as the missing piece that turns decentralized AI from a toy into infrastructure. A paid mesh network needs proof that a node actually ran the requested model or computation, not just a trust-me-bro GPU marketplace.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: Interpretability hooks and ZK proofs are framed as two paths toward making AI compute auditable and more fungible. If users can verify what a model did or prove that requested computation ran, marketplaces for distributed training and inference become much more viable.

title: 21 in 21: Mic Neale on goose, Mesh LLM, and Open Source AI
text: Mic says a paid shared-compute network needs trustworthy, safe, verifiable execution before users will fund priority LLM access and hardware owners can reliably earn from idle machines.

title: Bitcoin's Branding Problem, AI's Impact on Open Source, Can Spiral's Playbook Work for AI?
text: Bitcoin's brand problem shows up at the merchant layer: some sellers react emotionally against the word bitcoin before they understand the payment mechanics. The implication is that product framing, merchant education, and language may matter as much as technical rollout for mainstream acceptance.

title: The Brand of Bitcoin - Joshua Philippe (Fold) | Bitcoin Design Week
text: Joshua Philippe defines brand as the perception created by how bitcoin looks, talks, and shows up culturally, then argues bitcoin's open-source brand needs to mature beyond fragmented coins, orange tropes, and insider aesthetics.

title: Cash App Brand Design & Lessons for Branding Bitcoin - Kyle Fletcher (Block) | Bitcoin Design Week
text: Kyle Fletcher maps recent bitcoin aesthetics and asks designers to expand the creative vocabulary so bitcoin can reach the next 96% through everyday experiences rather than insider-coded visuals.

title: Bitcoin's Branding Problem, AI's Impact on Open Source, Can Spiral's Playbook Work for AI?
text: Open-source AI is treated as a category at risk of being captured by crypto-style grift if it lacks credible institutions and taste. The hosts want the bitcoin open-source playbook applied carefully, with funding focused on durable public goods rather than tokenized noise.

title: Strategy's STRC Buying Spree, Open-Source AI Blind Spots, Bitcoin Stablecoins from Utexo & Ark
text: The open-source AI funding question is framed through blind spots: work that big labs and VC-backed startups are unlikely to do because it is too infrastructural, too non-commercial, or too far from immediate customer capture. Spiral is floated as a possible funder if the problem selection is disciplined.

title: Meta Stablecoins Return, Open-Source Agents, OpenClaw Builder Meetup
text: Local open-source models are framed as a privacy and control layer that can sit between personal data and cloud frontier models. The opportunity is not just cheaper inference, but giving users their own agentic system that can decide what should stay local and what can safely leave the machine.

title: PBJ: Anthropic's Fable Drama, Personhood for AI, Bark Launches on Mainnet
text: The hosts map the AI stack across frontier model labs, infrastructure, data, and product layers, then land on excitement for stronger open models and open layers that can compete outside closed lab ecosystems.

title: Goose Developers on the Future of Open-Source AI Agents
text: The Goose talk treats local and open models as a practical part of the agent stack: privacy, lower latency, offline use, and no incremental per-token cost make open models useful even when frontier cloud models remain stronger.

title: PBJ: Announcing PB's Open Source AI Summit, Bitcoin Forks, Local AI Builder Recap
text: The Open Source AI Summit announcement defines the program around open models, local models, and the philosophy of open AI infrastructure. PBJ connects the summit to the Builder meetup and the localmaxxing movement.

title: PBJ: Goose Development Kit, Spiral Expands Into AI, Can Bitcoin Names Scale?
text: The hosts discuss how developers might orchestrate open-source models alongside Claude, Codex, and other frontier tools, with Buzz and Goose as possible coordination surfaces for mixed open and closed model workflows.

title: 21 in 21: 0xSero on Local AI, Open Models, and Benchmarking
text: 0xSero says each controversial move by a closed AI company produces a new wave of interest in systems that are distributed, publicly owned, and developed in the open.

title: 21 in 21: Bradley Axen on Buzz, goose, and AI at Block
text: Block helped found the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, contributing Goose alongside Anthropic's MCP and OpenAI's agents.md while helping develop shared protocols for the wider agent ecosystem.

title: Bitcoin's Branding Problem, AI's Impact on Open Source, Can Spiral's Playbook Work for AI?
text: Spiral's bitcoin playbook is tested against AI: fund small teams, protocol work, SDKs, and public goods that are unlikely to be run over by frontier labs. The open question is whether auditability, provenance, and low-level infrastructure give Spiral a comparable role in AI.

title: Bitcoin Acceptance on Square, Unpacking the Lava Drama, CashApp & Lightning Dollars
text: Spiral's merchant-adoption work is framed as activating bitcoin's volunteer army, something stablecoin companies and corporate chains cannot easily copy. The team shipped practical tools so local advocates can convince merchants, populate Bitcoin Map, and turn Square's rollout into visible payment behavior.

title: Coinbase Mortgages, Privacy for AI and Payments, Lexe Launches
text: Spiral's AI criteria focus on work that a small nonprofit team can defend: low-level tools, protocol work, SDKs, and public goods far enough from the customer that big labs are unlikely to steamroll them. The filter is impact without revenue dependence, borrowing the bitcoin open-source playbook for AI infrastructure.

title: Did Quantum FUD Price, Bitcoin Merchant Community, Competing with  Stripe
text: Spiral's wave two is a merchant-adoption toolkit rather than protocol work: one-pagers, plushies, and local champion boxes are meant to turn Square's bitcoin payment rollout into street-level action. The segment shows Spiral acting as a bridge between open-source infrastructure and grassroots distribution.

title: Goose Developers on the Future of Open-Source AI Agents
text: Steve explains why Goose is moving into Spiral: Spiral has seven years of public-goods and open-source credibility in bitcoin, and now wants to bring decentralization, permissionless technology, and open-source values to AI.

title: PBJ: Goose Development Kit, Spiral Expands Into AI, Can Bitcoin Names Scale?
text: Spiral's AI expansion is presented as additive to bitcoin rather than a retreat from it. Steve argues the AI audience is much larger today, and open-source, decentralized AI work can ultimately be a net win for bitcoin.

title: PBJ: Kimi K3 and the Open-Weight Race, AI Treasure Hunting, Bitcoin Falls Further Behind Gold
text: Although Loupe currently sits inside Spiral, Steve wants it to become an independent public good with its own contributors, reputation, and continuity. The goal is for Loupe to survive even if Spiral eventually disappears.

title: Strategy's STRC Buying Spree, Open-Source AI Blind Spots, Bitcoin Stablecoins from Utexo & Ark
text: STRC buying is presented as live financial engineering at scale: Strategy can sell hundreds of millions of dollars of overcollateralized bitcoin credit at roughly 11.5% yield. The hosts separate that capital-markets machine from technical bitcoin development, while acknowledging how much economic gravity it creates.

title: PBJ: Frontier Models Eating All, SF's AI Dominance, What Happened at Bitcoin Vegas
text: Saylor's Vegas explanation of STRC gives the hosts a cleaner frame for Stretch: a bitcoin-backed credit instrument that can sit between treasury accumulation and more money-like products.

title: Strategy's STRC Buying Spree, Open-Source AI Blind Spots, Bitcoin Stablecoins from Utexo & Ark
text: Bitcoin stablecoins are treated as a missing product category: Utexo and Ark-style designs point toward dollar instruments that use bitcoin rails or bitcoin credit without defaulting to Ethereum-style token platforms. The strategic question is whether bitcoin-native stablecoins can win on settlement, interoperability, or yield rather than ideology.

title: Codex vs Claude Vibe Coding, Study Shows AI Agents Prefer Bitcoin, Kazakhstan to Add BTC?
text: Codex is compared with Claude Code through real vibe-coding workflow: running CLI agents for hours, letting them plan and continue work, and using multiple coding agents against each other. The discussion treats coding agents as already practical infrastructure, not a demo category.

title: Codex vs Claude Vibe Coding, Study Shows AI Agents Prefer Bitcoin, Kazakhstan to Add BTC?
text: Vibe coding is pushed from desk workflow into ambient workflow: Max describes using Codex from a car ride, checking in every 10 or 15 minutes and telling the agent to continue. The point is that coding becomes supervision of an autonomous process rather than continuous hands-on implementation.

title: Our 2026 Predictions, Contentious Forks, Vibe Coding Community
text: The vibe-coding community is treated as an emerging production surface for Presidio Bitcoin ideas. A member-built app becomes evidence that PBJ brainstorms can turn into working software quickly, especially when AI can generate personalized interfaces and bounty-style projects.
